key_concepts: Circle Equidistance Definition: A circle is the set of all points in a plane equidistant (radius r) from a fixed center point O.
Compass as Length Transfer Tool: A compass transfers exact segment lengths accurately, avoiding parallax tick mark errors associated with rulers.
Concentric Circles: Circles drawn with different radii sharing the exact same central reference point.
Perpendicular Corner Construction: Using set-squares or compass arcs to construct 90° right angle corners for building rectangles and squares.
Inscribing Regular Hexagons: Stepping the compass opening (radius r) six times around a circle boundary constructs a regular hexagon of side length r.
core_summary: This chapter introduces precise technical geometric construction using ruler and compass. It covers drawing circles of specified radii, locating centers, transferring lengths accurately, constructing perpendiculars, building rectangles and squares, and creating symmetric geometric art.

key_terms.definition: A closed plane curve consisting of all points equidistant from a fixed central point.
The constant distance from the center point of a circle to any point on its circumference.
A straight line segment passing through the center of a circle with both endpoints on the circumference (d = 2r).
Circles of different radii that share the exact same central point.

key_takeaways: A compass is both a drawing tool for circles and a precision length transfer instrument.
A regular hexagon inscribed in a circle has a side length exactly equal to the circle's radius.
Holding the compass firmly by its top pivot prevents needle slippage during rotation.
